task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data isn't working properly — sometimes it stops working completely, and other times it's just very slow. I'd really like to get it fixed, please.

turns.thought:

To get started, I'll need to look up your account. Could you please provide either:
- the phone number associated with the line that's having trouble, or
- your customer ID?

(If it's easier, I can also look you up by your full name and date of birth.)
turns.execution_output: User: My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps!

turns.thought: Thanks, John! Let me look up your account now.

turns.thought:
Good news — I was able to find your account and identify the cause.

I found your line **555-123-2002** (line L1002) on the **Premium Plan**. Here's what I see:

- **Data used this cycle:** 15.1 GB
- **Plan data limit:** 15.0 GB
- **Billing cycle ends:** 2025-02-28

You've used up your monthly data allowance, which is why your mobile data is cutting out entirely or running very slowly. Your line status is Active and roaming is already enabled, so this isn't a service or roaming issue.

You have two options to restore full-speed data:

**Option 1 — Add more data (refuel)**
- The Premium Plan refueling rate is **$2.00 per GB**, added to your bill.
- The maximum you can add is **2 GB** (so $2.00–$4.00).
- This data lasts through the end of your current cycle (2025-02-28), then your allowance resets.

**Option 2 — Change to a plan with more data**

Which option would you prefer? If you'd like to refuel, just let me know how many GB you'd like (up to 2 GB) and I'll confirm the price before applying it.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh dear, I had no idea I'd used all my data... I don't want to change my plan though — that sounds complicated and I'm worried it would cost me more. 

So if I add that extra data, will my internet go back to being fast? I really need it to work well. But yes, let's go ahead and add the 2 GB, please. That's the most I can add, right?

turns.thought:
All done! I've added **2 GB** of data to your line **555-123-2002** for a total charge of **$4.00**, which will appear on your next bill.

Your data allowance is now 17 GB for this billing cycle (15 GB plan limit + 2 GB refueled), and your cycle ends **February 28, 2025** — at which point your allowance resets back to the standard 15 GB.

You're correct that 2 GB is the maximum that can be added at one time.

Since you mentioned your data was stopping completely and running slowly, I'd suggest a couple of quick checks on your end to make sure everything is running smoothly now:

- **Restart your phone** — this helps the device reconnect to the network and pick up the new allowance.
- If it's still slow, check whether **Data Saver** is turned on in your settings, as that can reduce speeds.

Can you try using your mobile data now and let me know if it's back to normal? If it's still not working well, I'm happy to keep troubleshooting with you.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh, a restart? That makes me nervous — I have so many photos of my grandchildren on this phone. Will restarting it delete any of my pictures? I don't want to lose those...

Also, you mentioned two things — restarting and checking that Data Saver thing. I'm afraid I can only do one thing at a time, I get confused easily. Which one should I do first?

turns.thought:
Please don't worry — a restart will **not** delete your photos. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on again; it doesn't remove any of your pictures, messages, or apps. Your photos of your grandchildren will be perfectly safe.

To answer your second question: **do the restart first.**

Here's why: a restart lets your phone reconnect to the network and recognize the 2 GB of data I just added. Often that alone fixes the problem, and you might not need the second step at all.

So:
1. Press and hold the power button, then choose **Restart** (or "Restart" / "Reboot" on screen).
2. Wait for the phone to turn back on (a minute or two).
3. Try your mobile data — open a web page or an app that uses the internet.

Once that's done, come back and tell me how it's working. If it's still slow, I'll walk you through checking Data Saver as a second step — one thing at a time, just as you'd like.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, you've reassured me about the photos. Let me try restarting it now... here goes.

turns.thought:
You haven't broken anything — please don't worry! Airplane Mode is just a setting that turns off all the wireless connections on your phone, and it's very easy to switch back off. Nothing is damaged or lost.

Here's the simplest way to turn it off:

1. **From the top of your screen, swipe downward** with one finger — this opens your Quick Settings panel.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** (it looks like a little airplane ✈️). It's probably highlighted or glowing because it's on.
3. **Tap that airplane icon once** so it's no longer highlighted.

That's it! After a few moments you should see your signal bars return at the top of the screen, and your mobile data should come back on.

One extra step just to be sure — after Airplane Mode is off, please **turn mobile data back on** in that same Quick Settings panel. Look for the icon labeled **Mobile data** (or "Cellular data") and tap it so it's switched on. Airplane Mode being on had switched it off, so we want to switch it back on.

Take your time with each step, and once you've done both, try opening a web page or an app that uses the internet. Then come back and tell me how it's going — if it's working, we're all set; if not, I'll keep helping you, one step at a time.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try turning off that Airplane Mode first. One thing at a time, like you said.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's exactly the one I mentioned! "Data Saver" is a setting that reduces your data usage, but it can make your internet feel slow or cause apps to misbehave.

It's safe to turn off, and since you now have that extra 2 GB of data, you don't need it restricting things.

Here's how:

1. **Swipe down from the top of your screen** again, just like you did before, to open Quick Settings.
2. Look for the **Data Saver** icon (it may have a downward arrow 🔽 or just say "Data Saver").
3. **Tap it once** so it's no longer highlighted or switched on.

If you don't see it there, you can also find it in **Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver**, and switch it off there.

Once that's done, try your internet again — open a web page or an app that needs data. Let me know how it works now, and if things are running smoothly, we're all finished. If it's still slow, I'll keep helping you with the next step.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn that Data Saver off.

turns.thought:
That's great news — your status bar showing **signal, 5G, and data enabled** means your phone is connected to the network properly, and on the fastest type of network available. That's exactly what we wanted to see.

I'm not able to run a speed test from my end, but the simplest way for you to check is just to **use the internet the way you normally would**:

- Open your web browser and load a page you visit often.
- Or open an app that uses data, like your email or a news app.

If pages come up quickly and the little loading bar moves right along, your data is working well. If you'd like a more formal check, you can type **"speed test"** into your web browser's search box and there are free websites that will measure it for you — but honestly, your 5G indicator and normal browsing will tell you what you need to know.

So to recap what we did together today:
1. ✅ Added **2 GB** of data to your line 555-123-2002 ($4.00 on your next bill) — you were over your 15 GB limit, which was the original cause.
2. ✅ Turned **Airplane Mode off**.
3. ✅ Turned **mobile data back on**.
4. ✅ Turned **Data Saver off**.

Give it a try and let me know how it feels. If it's running well, we're all done — and remember, your allowance resets to 15 GB on **February 28**. If it's still sluggish, I'm right here and we'll keep going one step at a time.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try that speed test thing you mentioned...

turns.thought:
You didn't do anything wrong — please don't worry! The good news is that your phone **is** connected to the network, since you're seeing 5G and "data enabled" in your status bar. So we've definitely made progress. A failed speed test just means we have one more small thing to track down.

Let's take it one step at a time, as you prefer.

**First, let's check if your phone is using Wi-Fi instead of mobile data.** This is actually the most common reason a speed test fails — if your phone is connected to a Wi-Fi network that doesn't have working internet, the speed test will say "No Connection" even though your mobile data is perfectly fine.

Here's what to do:

1. **Swipe down from the top of your screen** to open Quick Settings again.
2. Look for the **Wi-Fi** icon (it looks like a little fan or扇形 shape).
3. **Is it highlighted/on, and does it show a network name?** 

- If it shows a network name you recognize (like "Home" or a neighbor's name), **tap the Wi-Fi icon once to turn it OFF.** This forces your phone to use your mobile data instead.
- Then try the speed test again.

Come back and tell me what you see — whether Wi-Fi was on, and whether the speed test works now with it off.

If Wi-Fi was already off and the test still fails, don't worry at all. We'll move to the next step: checking your APN settings (the settings your phone uses to connect to our data network), which is another easy fix. We'll get there together, one step at a time.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the Wi-Fi for you.

turns.thought: Good — that rules out Wi-Fi. Let me take a quick look at your device details on my end while I explain the next step.

turns.thought:
Perfect — thank you for checking, and yes, APN settings is a good next step. I'll walk you through it.

**What is an APN?** It stands for "Access Point Name." It's simply the address your phone uses to connect to our mobile data network. If it's missing or incorrect, you can have full 5G signal and data switched on, but web pages and speed tests still won't load — which matches exactly what you're experiencing.

Let's check it together. Take your time:

1. Open your **Settings** app (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (on some phones this is called **Connections** or **Mobile Network**).
3. Tap **Mobile Network**, then look for **Access Point Names** (or just **APN**) and tap it.
4. You should see a list with one entry selected. **Don't edit or delete anything** — just look at what's there.
5. Now tap the **three dots** in the top-right corner (or the menu button), and choose **Reset to default**.
6. After it resets, **restart your phone** again — this is important, as the new settings only take effect after a restart.
7. Once it's back on, try the speed test or a web page again.

A couple of reassurances:
- Using "Reset to default" is safe. It simply restores the correct settings — **it will not delete your photos, messages, or apps.**
- If the list of APNs looks completely empty, that's actually a useful clue too — just tell me and we'll go from there.

Give that a try and let me know what happens. If the internet works, we're done and you're all set. If it still says "No Connection," please tell me whether the APN list had an entry in it or was empty — and at that point I'll bring in our technical support specialists, who have additional tools to run deeper checks on your line from their end. We'll get this sorted out.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll try to reset those APN settings. You're sure it won't delete my photos, right? Okay... let me do it.

turns.thought:
Thank you for checking that — and yes, that actually looks correct! An APN named **"internet"** along with a web address for picture messages (that's the MMSC) is exactly what a healthy configuration looks like. So that's good news, and it also tells me your phone's basic network address is fine.

Since that's correct but you're still getting "No Connection," the next step is to have your phone **refresh those settings** anyway. Sometimes settings look right on screen but are stale behind the scenes, and a refresh plus a restart clears it up. It's completely safe:

1. Go back to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network → Access Point Names**.
2. Tap the **three dots** in the top-right corner.
3. Choose **Reset to default**.
4. **Restart your phone** (press and hold the power button, then tap Restart).
5. Once it's back on, try the speed test again.

Two reassurances:
- This **will not delete** your photos, texts, or apps — it only refreshes network settings.
- After the restart, please double-check at the top of your screen that you still see **5G** and that **Airplane Mode is off** (it came back on last time, so it's worth a glance). After a restart, your device may need you to turn mobile data back on as well.

Please try that and let me know the result.

And please don't worry — you haven't done anything wrong at any point. You've been following my instructions carefully, and this is just a case of working through the possible causes one at a time. If this doesn't do it, I have a couple more things we can try on your device, and I can also involve our technical support specialists who have additional tools to test your line directly from their end. We'll get your data working.
turns.execution_output:
User: But... I already did that. I reset the APN settings and restarted, and it still said "No Connection." That was exactly what we just did. 

I'm sorry, I'm just getting a bit upset — I've restarted my phone twice now and done all these steps, and my internet still doesn't work. Is there something else we can try? I really don't want to keep doing the same thing over and over.

turns.thought:
You're absolutely right, and I apologize — I should have recognized we'd already done that step. Let's move on to something new right away.

Let me check one more setting on your phone, and this one is a likely culprit:

**Network mode preference.** Your phone can be set to prefer older, slower network types like 2G or 3G. If it's locked to one of those, you can have what looks like a connection but no actual data — which matches your symptoms exactly.

**Please do this:**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (or **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile Network**.
4. Look for **Preferred network mode** (it may be called **Network mode**).
5. **Tell me what it currently says** — don't change it yet.

If it says **2G** or **3G**, tap it and choose **5G/4G preferred** (or the option that includes 5G or LTE). That should restore your data speed.

I know this has been frustrating, and you've been very patient doing all these steps. I promise this is a different step from what we've tried.

Let me know what that setting says — and if it already says 5G, tell me that too, because at that point I'll bring in our technical support specialists. They have additional tools to test your line directly from their end and can dig deeper than I can, which sounds like the right move given everything you've already tried.

Also, just so you know: your account and line look perfectly healthy from my side — Active status, roaming enabled, and the 2 GB I added is showing correctly. So this is likely a device-level setting we can still fix together.
